definition: A decoding algorithm that keeps track of multiple candidate sequences ('beams') at each generation step, rather than committing to a single most likely token.
details: Beam search often produces more globally coherent text than greedy decoding by considering several likely continuations in parallel, though it can sometimes produce repetitive or generic outputs.
story: Imagine a sketch artist who starts with static and, stroke by stroke, sharpens it into a face. The result feels creative because it is memory, reshuffled at speed. Given a starting line, the machine imagines what comes next — a word, a note, a patch of a picture. The model dreams a little, then cleans up the dream. And that is Beam Search — making something new out of everything it has ever seen.
